context: A uni student interviews a retired diplomat about overseas postings
purpose: Teach: 中国人/インドネシア/中国語/トルコ/フィリピン/ポルトガル/エジプト/パレスチナ

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 本日はお時間ありがとうございます。最初の海外赴任はインドネシア出張から始まったと伺いました。
lines.en: Thank you for your time today. I heard your first overseas posting began with a business trip to Indonesia.
lines.style: Polite interviewer opening, formal university student tone, respectful and slightly nervous.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: そうだね。三月半ばに辞令が出て、まだ中国語学習を始めたばかりの頃だったよ。
lines.en: That's right. The orders came in mid-March, back when I had just started studying Chinese.
lines.style: Reflective elder statesman, warm reminiscing tone, measured pace with gentle nostalgia.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: その後、トルコ航空でエジプト旅行も兼ねた赴任地へ移られたんですよね。職務経歴が本当に華やかです。
lines.en: After that, you moved to your next posting via Turkish Airlines, combined with a trip through Egypt. Your career history is truly impressive.
lines.style: Admiring student voice, eager curiosity, slight excitement breaking through formality.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: 華やかに見えるかもしれんが、パレスチナ問題の現場に突入した時は本当に怖かった。現金払いしか通じない地域も多くてね。
lines.en: It may look glamorous, but when I was thrown into the middle of the Palestinian issue, it was truly frightening. Many areas only accepted cash payment.
lines.style: Sobering elder tone, weight of experience, candid honesty replacing earlier warmth.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 想像もつきません。フィリピン料理やポルトガル料理など、各地の食文化も研究されたと聞きました。
lines.en: I can't even imagine. I heard you also researched local food cultures, like Filipino and Portuguese cuisine.
lines.style: Gentle pivot to lighter topic, genuine curiosity, conversational warmth returning.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: ああ、食べ歩きが唯一の趣味でね。中国人留学生の友人と毎週火曜日に集まって、料金値上げの前に名店を巡ったものだ。
lines.en: Ah yes, food touring was my one hobby. I'd meet a Chinese exchange student friend every Tuesday and visit famous restaurants before any price hikes.
lines.style: Fondly amused elder, chuckling memories, light playful tone of nostalgic friendship.

lines.speaker: ren_uni
lines.jp: 素敵ですね。最後に、これから外交官を目指す学生へ一言いただけますか。
lines.en: How wonderful. Finally, could you give a word of advice to students who want to become diplomats?
lines.style: Closing the interview, sincere reverence, slight formal tightening before final question.

lines.speaker: hiroshi_elder
lines.jp: お金を稼ぐ仕事ではない。だが、語学を一つ、できれば二つ深く学びなさい。それが君の一生の財産になるよ。
lines.en: It's not a job for earning money. But study one language deeply, ideally two. That will become a lifelong asset.
lines.style: Grandfatherly closing wisdom, slow deliberate cadence, heartfelt advice with quiet conviction.
